title: Beyond Update Counts: A Control Map for Evaluating Test-Time Model Updates
abstract: arXiv:2610.36109v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Test-time updating lets a language model change persistent state after training---such as model weights, adapter parameters, or a memory module---before or while answering queries. Existing evaluations often compare systems using update count or frequency and performance measured immediately afterward. These summaries omit what is updated, where, when, and in what order. The same total can therefore hide an important difference: one system may answer after one update while another answers after two. We introduce the Control Map, an evaluation framework that records the committed updates preceding each scored answer and separately evaluates behavioral changes, immediate learning (acquisition), later recall (retention), preservation of unrelated behavior (locality), and performance in new settings. translated_title: 超越更新次数：一种用于评估测试时模型更新的控制图
translated_abstract: 测试时更新使语言模型能够在训练之后、回答查询之前或回答过程中改变其持久状态——例如模型权重、适配器参数或记忆模块。现有评估方法通常仅通过更新次数或更新频率，以及之后立即测量的性能来比较系统。这些概括遗漏了更新了什么、在哪里更新、何时更新以及以何种顺序更新。因此，相同的总次数可能掩盖一个重要差异：一个系统可能在一次更新后作答，而另一个系统在两次更新后才作答。我们提出了控制图，这是一个评估框架，它记录每次评分答案之前所提交的更新，并分别评估行为变化、即时学习（习得）、后续回忆（保持）、无关行为的保留（局部性）以及在全新环境中的表现。我们证明了在何种条件下仅凭更新次数即可确定最终状态，并在给定假设下展示了答案前更新历史的差异如何限制可测……
tldr: 提出控制图评估框架，通过记录每次作答前的完整更新历史，分别评估即时学习、记忆保持、局部性与新环境泛化，从而超越仅凭更新次数比较测试时模型更新的局限。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces the Control Map, an evaluation framework that records the full history of committed updates preceding each scored answer, enabling separate assessment of acquisition, retention, locality, and generalization beyond mere update counts for test-time model updates.
